screening_decisions.reason: Randomized trial where surgeons were assigned to receive patient preference report (PROMs feedback) detailing patient goals and treatment preferences vs administering usual care. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.

Randomized controlled trial testing hypothesis that informing dentists about patients' dental anxiety (PROMs) prior to treatment reduces patient anxiety. Intervention group: dentist informed of MDAS score; Control: dentist not informed. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.

Randomized controlled trial investigating effects of session-by-session progress feedback using ultra-brief Outcome Rating Scale (PROMs) vs no feedback. Participants randomly assigned to 'feedback' or 'no feedback' status. Directly compares PROMs feedback to therapists vs not providing such information.

Stepped wedge randomized controlled trial comparing continuous feedback on patient progress during therapy to therapist and supervisor (MeMOS condition) vs only given to the therapist (S-Sup condition). This compares PROMs feedback in supervision vs feedback to therapists alone.

Randomized controlled trial of web-based eHealth application that supports survivors in self-management by monitoring HRQOL and symptoms and obtaining tailored feedback with personalized overview of supportive care options. Intervention: access to Oncokompas with PROMs feedback; Control: delayed access. Directly compares PROMs feedback to patients vs not providing such information.
Integrated literature review, not a randomized trial. Does not meet inclusion criteria for study design.

Randomized controlled trial comparing standard care to standard care supplemented with mobile telehealth including self-monitoring, mobile-phone data transmissions, and graphical and nurse-initiated feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.

Randomized controlled trial with three arms: (1) regular completion of HRQL questionnaires with feedback of results to physicians, (2) completion of questionnaires but no feedback, (3) no HRQL measurement. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.

Randomized trial where depressed patients were randomized to be identified as clinically depressed to their physician vs not identified (control). Self-rating depression scale (PROMs) was administered and feedback to physicians was compared to no feedback.
Laboratory study on driving impairment and self-efficacy in DUI offenders. Not a clinical PROMs feedback study comparing PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals/patients vs no feedback.

Randomized trial where physicians were randomized to demonstration arm (receiving reporting system for summarizing anxiety symptom levels and functioning status) vs control arm. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.
Validation study of SF-36 questionnaire using postal questionnaire design. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Randomized controlled trial with Featback intervention consisting of psychoeducation and a fully automated monitoring- and feedback system. Compared to waiting list. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Randomized controlled trial where experimental group physicians received reports summarizing patients' responses to functional disability questionnaire, while control group physicians received no report. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.

Randomized trial comparing home monitoring conditions including symptom monitoring with feedback vs peak flow training without feedback vs no peak flow training. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Feasibility study of multimodal supportive care intervention targeting unmet needs. Abstract does not clearly describe PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals or patients vs no feedback. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
Structured/systematic review, not a randomized trial. Does not meet inclusion criteria for study design.
Database analysis of VTE risk in immune-mediated diseases. Not a randomized trial and not about PROMs feedback.

Randomized trial where case coordinators were assigned to experimental condition (pain assessment battery with summary sent to physicians via mail/fax) vs control condition (assessed as usual). Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.

Abstract describes building and validating a psychometric tool to screen self-care activities in general population during COVID-19 lockdown. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals/patients vs no feedback.

Randomized controlled trial where one group received WSQ intervention with physicians' feedback vs controls received treatment as usual. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.

Randomized trial comparing telephone monitoring of distress (TM) with educational materials (EM) vs EM alone. TM group patients were called monthly to monitor distress using HADS and EORTC-QLQ-C30, with referrals if scores above cutoff. Directly compares PROMs monitoring/feedback vs no feedback.

Randomized clinical trial comparing patient feedback system OQ-Analyst using Outcome Questionnaire-45.2 (feedback condition) vs no feedback. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs not providing such information.

Pilot randomized trial of app that facilitates weekly symptom reporting (via ESAS) and presents information cards and recommendations for supportive care services based on symptoms. Intervention arm vs control arm. Directly compares PROMs feedback to patients vs no feedback.

Cross-sectional mixed-methods study evaluating interpretability of PRO data presentation formats. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals/patients vs no feedback on outcomes.

Randomized clinical trial where intervention group additionally underwent a feedback session based on a knowledge test vs control group receiving routine preoperative patient education. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
Semi-structured qualitative interview study with GPs. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Feasibility cluster-randomised trial of self-management programme based on self-efficacy principles. Abstract does not clearly describe PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals or patients vs no feedback.

Randomized trial where patients completed PRIME-MD screening and were randomized to: (1) patient and physician told PRIME-MD results, (2) patient told PRIME-MD results, (3) neither told PRIME-MD results. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
Protocol/design paper describing rationale and implementation challenges of a clinical trial. Not a completed trial with results comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Randomized controlled trial with three conditions: usual care; HRQL assessment; HRQL assessment followed by structured interview and discussion (interpretive assistance). Directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

Randomized trial where for two-thirds of patients, self-reported cancer needs, QOL, and psychosocial information was made available to health care team who coordinated targeted psychosocial interventions; for one-third, information was not seen. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
Protocol paper describing study design. Not a completed trial with results comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
This is a self-help intervention with automated self-monitoring and feedback to patients themselves, not PROMs feedback to healthcare providers in clinical practice.
This is a scoping review on quality of care and multimorbidity, not a randomised controlled trial comparing PROMs feedback.
RCT comparing PROMs feedback (patient-reported outcomes data) to telephone caseworkers or oncologists/GPs versus usual care. Meets all selection criteria.
This is a methodological paper about measuring inconsistency in meta-analyses, not an RCT on PROMs feedback.
RCT comparing QoL questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30/LC13) with feedback during clinic versus no feedback/control. PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
RCT with systematic variation of screening, sensitization, and informational feedback to physicians about depression screening results.
This is an exploratory interview study with oncologists about their perspectives on QoL, not a randomised trial.
This is a meta-analysis on feedback interventions in general, not a primary RCT on PROMs feedback in clinical practice.
RCT with health status reports (AIMS/MHAQ) provided to physicians versus control. PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
RCT with pain scale summary provided to oncologists versus control. PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
This is about developing a tool (EMPRO) for assessing PRO measures, not an RCT on PROMs feedback in clinical practice.
This is about tobacco cessation counseling by pharmacists, not PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
This is a theory-driven review paper discussing applications of PROs, not a primary RCT.
Pilot RCT with daily electronic symptom reporting (PROs) to nurses in inpatient setting versus control.
RCT with automated symptom monitoring and email alerts to clinical team for severe symptoms versus no alerts.
RCT with GHQ (General Health Questionnaire) results provided to clinicians versus no feedback.
RCT with patient self-assessment of disease activity (DAS) reported to treating rheumatologist versus control.
RCT with OQ-45 (Outcome Questionnaire) feedback to clinicians versus control in psychiatric outpatient population.
RCT with web-mediated follow-up based on weekly self-scored patient symptoms with alert emails to oncologist versus routine follow-up.
This is about developing a patient-reported outcome measure (NFI-MND), not an RCT on PROMs feedback.
This is about personality testing feedback, not health-related PROMs feedback for clinical outcomes.
This is a review/discussion paper on PROs pathways, not a primary RCT.
RCT with HRQL questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30) graphic summary to physicians and patients versus control.
RCT with PROMIS symptom scores visual display to clinicians versus scores not provided.
RCT with QoL assessment feedback to clinicians versus standard assessment versus assessment without feedback.
Pilot RCT with PediQUEST survey reports to oncologists and families versus no feedback.
This is about developmental screening tools for children, not PROMs feedback about patient health outcomes.
RCT with QoL profile and expert report sent to coordinating practitioner versus standard care.
This is a commentary on a quality monitoring project, not a primary RCT on PROMs feedback.
RCT with electronic Lung Cancer Symptom Scale data provided to oncologist versus standard clinical assessment alone.
RCT with GHQ results provided to emergency physicians versus control.
RCT with disclosure of Beck depression inventory scores to general practitioners versus no disclosure.
RCT with ESRA-C graphical summary provided to clinical team versus no summary.

Randomized controlled trial comparing a flare management intervention using the FLARE-RA questionnaire (PROM) with feedback to non-physician providers versus usual care. The PROM results were used to guide nursing counseling or expedited visits. Meets criteria for PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
This is a descriptive/editorial article describing examples of PROMs use in practice, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.
This is a review/framework paper discussing implementation of PROs in clinical practice, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

This is an RCT of a short-term life review therapeutic intervention, not a PROMs feedback intervention. The intervention is a psychological therapy, not feedback on patient-reported outcome measurements.

Randomized controlled trial comparing communication of PC-SAD screening results with offer of psychiatric evaluation versus no feedback on test result. This is PROMs/screening feedback to patients with comparison to no feedback.

This RCT evaluates a depression care management program (algorithm-based care, psychotherapy, medication monitoring), not PROMs feedback. The intervention is comprehensive care management, not feedback on patient-reported outcomes.

Randomized trial comparing systematic screening for AED adverse effects using AEP scores (PROM) made available to treating physicians versus not made available. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.

Randomized controlled trial of the Partners for Change Outcome Management System (PCOMS), a continuous outcome feedback system provided to therapists versus no-feedback condition. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.

Cluster randomized controlled trial evaluating a mobile/web-based monitoring and feedback tool combined with self-management support versus usual care. The tool collects patient data and provides feedback, meeting PROMs feedback criteria.

Randomized trial comparing different feedback conditions on PCS screening results (more symptoms than average, fewer symptoms than average, neutral) versus each other. This tests effects of PROMs screening feedback on outcomes.

Cluster randomized trial comparing electronic previsit questionnaires with youth violence questions (results delivered to physicians) versus without YV questions. PVQ results were provided to physicians before visits, constituting PROMs feedback to providers.

Randomized controlled trial comparing QoL-monitor assessing QoL, distress and care needs with feedback to patients and HCPs versus usual care. PROMs results were shown in medical files and discussed, meeting criteria.

Randomized trial comparing disclosure of composite screening questionnaire (SQ) results to GPs versus blinded (not disclosed). The SQ includes scales for somatisation, anxiety, depression and alcohol abuse. This is PROMs feedback to providers.
This is a methodological paper developing a classification system for PRO measures, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

Cluster randomized controlled trial comparing providing physicians with alcohol screening results (CAGE questionnaire, alcohol consumption, readiness to change) and recommendations versus control. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
Based on the abstract, this appears to be a systematic review protocol (cochranelibrary.com reference, objectives stated as 'To assess the effects'), not a primary randomized controlled trial.

Title suggests an RCT with feedback intervention for sun protection. While the abstract is truncated, the title indicates daily feedback (likely PROMs-based) as an intervention. Being conservative, I include this for full review.

Pilot cluster randomized controlled trial of Loop, a web-based communication tool that includes symptom reporting (patient self-reported measures). The tool facilitates communication around care management with patient-reported data, meeting criteria for PROMs feedback.
Cluster randomized controlled trial comparing surgeons receiving peer benchmarked PROMs feedback and education versus control. This directly tests PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.
Randomized controlled trial comparing feedback regarding patient progress to therapists versus no feedback. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers (therapists) during psychotherapy.

Randomized controlled trial comparing providing GPs with results of self-administered computerized assessment (PROQSY) of common mental disorders versus no additional information or GHQ results. This is PROMs feedback to providers.
Randomized trial comparing systematic monitoring of HRQOL (KIDSCREEN-27) with face-to-face discussion between patient and physician versus usual care. This is PROMs feedback in clinical practice.

Cluster randomized trial implementing STarT Back risk-stratification strategy using patient-reported data (STarT Back Tool) to categorize risk and guide treatment versus control. This uses PROMs to guide clinical decision-making.

Randomized controlled trial of recovery-focused intervention including pre-diagnostic wellbeing assessment (WHO Wellbeing Index - a PROM) with written feedback and post-diagnostic support. This includes PROMs feedback.
This is a guidance document from the Medical Research Council about evaluating complex interventions, not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

Randomized controlled trial comparing computer-generated feedback letters (based on screening results) versus in-person counseling versus assessment only. The computer-generated feedback arm tests PROMs feedback intervention.

This is a protocol for a non-inferiority trial comparing different methods of PROMs administration (telephone, postal, online, face-to-face). It does not test PROMs feedback intervention versus no feedback.
Randomized controlled trial comparing routine use of MOS SF-36 Health Survey with results given to physicians before encounter versus withheld. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.

Randomized clinical trial comparing electronic screening and personalized feedback with clinical decision support versus usual care. This is PROMs screening with feedback to both patients and clinicians.
This is a realist synthesis (systematic review methodology), not a randomized controlled trial. Does not meet the study design criterion.

Randomized trial comparing a computerized system where patients report symptoms and preferences prior to consultation, with information provided to patient and clinician versus control. This is PROMs feedback to providers.

Randomized trial comparing systematic screening with AEP (Adverse Events Profile, a PROM) where clinicians received the AEP results versus usual care without AEP. This is PROMs feedback to healthcare providers.

RCT comparing standard care to MTH intervention that includes graphical and nurse-initiated feedback on self-monitoring data. The intervention involves PROMs (self-efficacy, illness beliefs, self-care) feedback to patients.
RCT with 3 arms: treatment as usual, therapist feedback, and patient-therapist feedback. Directly compares PROMs progress information feedback vs no feedback on treatment outcomes.
This is a psychometric validation study for a new questionnaire (Hemofilia-QoL), not an RCT testing PROMs feedback effects on outcomes.
Cluster RCT where oncologists received immediate print-out LoMoS (patient-reported symptom monitoring) vs not. Directly compares PROMs feedback to clinicians vs no feedback.
Group RCT where clinicians received tailored longitudinal symptom reports and management suggestions (SAMI) vs usual care. Involves PROMs feedback to clinicians.
RCT evaluating real-time daily patient feedback to physicians with coaching. Involves patient-reported experience/quality feedback to providers.
RCT where physicians were given depression screening results (PROMs) to see if it altered medical record notation. Compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback to physicians.
This is a Cochrane review protocol/summary, not an individual RCT testing PROMs feedback.
RCT comparing feedback about patient's mental health problem and desires vs control. Involves PROMs feedback to physicians.
RCT comparing symptom monitoring plus feedback (SM+F) vs usual care. Involves PROMs feedback to providers.
RCT with computer-generated feedback to physicians about patient's functional status (PROMs) vs control. Directly tests PROMs feedback effects.
RCT with 3 arms: feedback to therapist, feedback to therapist and patient, and no feedback. Directly compares PROMs outcome monitoring feedback vs no feedback.
RCT where intervention group completed monthly outcome questionnaires and received 3-monthly feedback vs treatment as usual. Directly tests PROMs feedback.
RCT evaluating addition of personalized feedback (on physical/psychological status, symptoms) to CBT self-help vs without feedback. Involves PROMs feedback to patients.
RCT investigating systematic symptom reporting by patients using Symptom Monitor. Involves PROMs monitoring with likely feedback component.
RCT where patients reported symptoms via tablets and physicians received symptom printouts at visits. Directly compares PROMs feedback vs usual care.
RCT comparing outcome monitoring feedback to therapists vs no-feedback control. Directly tests PROMs feedback effects.
RCT comparing video decision aid to standard educational materials for lung cancer screening decisions. Does not involve PROMs feedback intervention.
RCT of ISAR screening tool disclosure and nursing assessment vs usual care. ISAR is a risk screening tool, not a PROM. Does not involve PROMs feedback.
RCT where patients reported AEs weekly via electronic PRO-tool (PRO-CTCAE) vs standard monitoring. Involves PROMs reporting with feedback component.
RCT where intervention patients had symptom reports presented graphically with alerts during team rounds. Involves PROMs feedback to clinicians.
RCT comparing smartphone app (symptom and biomarker monitoring) vs standard face-to-face care. Involves PROMs monitoring component.
RCT giving RA patients access to Sanoia platform for self-assessment and self-monitoring vs usual care. Involves PROMs self-monitoring.
RCT with ecological momentary assessments and texting-based feedback on alcohol consumption. Involves PROMs feedback to patients.
Cluster RCT where patients and clinicians received continuous feedback of outcome via weekly computerised assessments vs no feedback. Directly tests PROMs feedback.
RCT where intervention physicians were provided patient's HAM-D depression scores and treatment recommendations vs no scores. Involves PROMs feedback to physicians.
RCT of web-based app for real-time symptom monitoring with alerts vs app without reminders. Involves PROMs monitoring component.
RCT where IVR system asked patients to rate pain/symptoms and oncologists received email alerts for moderate-severe symptoms. Involves PROMs feedback to physicians.
Psychometric development and validation study of ADDQoL questionnaire, not an RCT testing PROMs feedback effects.
Cluster RCT comparing generic feedback and patient-specific feedback strategies vs no feedback on end-of-life outcomes. Directly tests PROMs feedback.
Development and progress report of the PROMIS initiative, not an RCT testing PROMs feedback effects on outcomes.
RCT comparing nurse-led telephone follow-up vs hospital follow-up. Does not involve PROMs feedback intervention - compares follow-up methods.

RCT where physicians received patient-specific treatment recommendations based on PROMs (CES-D, HAM-D) screening vs control physicians with no intervention. Measured patient outcomes (HAM-D, SIP scores). Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers with no feedback.

RCT where intervention group received assessment summary displaying patients' self-reported symptoms to physicians/nurses, while control group did not. Measured symptom distress and need for symptom management support. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers with no feedback.

RCT with experimental group receiving ESM self-monitoring combined with weekly feedback sessions vs control group receiving treatment as usual. Measures patient empowerment. Compares PROMs feedback to patients with no feedback.

RCT comparing Nintendo Wii rehabilitation vs conventional physical therapy. The 'feedback' is device feedback during therapy, not PROMs feedback to patients or providers. Compares two active interventions, not PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

RCT comparing treatment as usual vs feedback condition where treatment progress and alliance information was provided to both clients and therapists. Directly compares PROMs feedback to patients and providers with no feedback.
Validation study of Dartmouth COOP Charts assessing reliability, validity, and clinical utility. Not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback. Does not meet study design criteria.

RCT where patients randomly assigned to receive feedback about PROMIS Pain Interference CAT prior to visit vs not receiving feedback. Measured patient satisfaction and communication. Directly compares PROMs feedback to patients with no feedback.

Study examining feedback regarding client progress and clinical support tools in psychotherapy. Reports feedback plus CST group had superior outcomes vs comparison. Appears to be an RCT comparing PROMs feedback to no feedback.
This is a systematic review of randomized clinical trials, not a primary randomized trial itself. Does not meet the study design criteria for inclusion.

Randomized controlled trial where practices received feedback of patient asthma information (morbidity, health services use, drug use) vs no feedback. Measured asthma symptoms, health services use, and drug use. Directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare providers with no feedback.
Commentary/opinion article discussing NHS Outcomes Framework and challenges of using PROMs at population level. Not a randomized trial. Does not meet study design criteria.

RCT where PRIME-MD results were provided to physicians (report group) vs not provided (no-report group). Measured psychiatric diagnosis, consultation, and referral rates. Directly compares PROMs diagnostic feedback to healthcare providers with no feedback.

Study used stratified random assignment to compare physician and patient reaction to SIP (Sickness Impact Profile). Half of physicians reviewed patient's SIP immediately prior to visit vs not. Examines effect of PROMs feedback on physician awareness and communication. Appears to meet criteria.

Study where 29 physicians used Dartmouth COOP Charts to measure patient health status during clinical encounter vs 27 control clinicians using no measure. Compared process of care and patient satisfaction. Directly compares PROMs assessment/feedback with no assessment.

RCT comparing standard mHealth (IVR calls with clinician alerts) vs mHealth+CP (same intervention plus automated emails with patient status feedback to CarePartner). Measured medication adherence, symptoms, and quality of life. Compares PROMs feedback to informal caregiver with standard care.

RCT comparing stellate ganglion block (SGB) procedure vs sham procedure for PTSD treatment. Measures PROMs (CAPS, depression, anxiety) as outcomes, but does not test PROMs feedback to patients or providers. Tests a medical intervention, not PROMs feedback.

This is a feasibility randomised controlled trial (partly individually randomised, partly cluster-randomised) comparing PROMs monitoring with feedback to patients (determined by practitioners) versus control. While it\'s a feasibility study, it meets the core criteria of being a randomised trial comparing PROMs feedback versus no feedback on depression outcomes.

This is a randomised trial where participants were randomized into a feedback group (clinicians received clinical feedback reports at intake and 6 weeks) versus a control group (clinicians received no report). This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus no feedback on mental health outcomes.

This is a cluster randomised controlled trial testing the DIALOG intervention where patients rated quality of life and treatment needs, with responses fed back immediately in screen displays and discussed with clinicians versus treatment as usual. This directly compares PROMs feedback to both patients and clinicians versus no feedback.

This is an observational study examining HRQoL in overweight youth participating in weight management interventions. It does not test PROMs feedback versus no feedback, and is not a randomised trial comparing feedback interventions. It focuses on weight management outcomes, not PROMs feedback effects.

This is a randomised clinical trial testing the ability of feedback of screening instrument results (General Health Questionnaire) to increase clinician awareness of patient emotional/psychological problems versus no feedback. This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals versus no feedback.

This is a randomised trial (370 patients randomly assigned) comparing treatment progress information and clinical decision-support tools (feedback to both patients and therapists) versus treatment-as-usual. This directly compares PROMs feedback to both parties versus no feedback.

This is a randomised controlled study where patients in the intervention group completed a depression self-rating scale (Montgomery-Asberg) at each GP consultation, with GPs using the completed instrument as basis for person-centred discussion versus treatment as usual. This directly compares PROMs feedback to clinicians versus no feedback.

This is a systematic review of controlled trials, not a primary randomised trial itself. The review identifies 21 studies but does not present original trial data comparing PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

This is a randomised controlled trial comparing assessments of physical function with feedback to both participant and physician versus functional assessments alone (no feedback). This directly compares PROMs feedback to both parties versus no feedback.
This is a review/guidance paper summarizing the ISOQOL User\'s Guide for implementing PROs in clinical practice. It is not a randomised trial and does not test PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

This is a qualitative, formative evaluation using semi-structured interviews and focus groups to explore GP views on using mental health questionnaires. It is not a randomised trial and does not provide quantitative outcomes comparing PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

This is a study protocol only, not the completed trial results. The protocol describes a planned RCT comparing web-based CBT with protocol-driven feedback versus support on demand versus wait list, but no actual trial data is presented.
This is a bibliographic study examining the growth and availability of quality of life measures across specialties. It is not a randomised trial testing PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

This is a randomised controlled trial (51 children randomized) comparing the eSAID electronic survey (children report feelings and coping preferences to dentists via a 26-item questionnaire) versus a control version with only 2 items. This directly compares PROMs feedback to clinicians versus minimal/no feedback.

This is a randomised controlled trial (461 outpatients randomized) comparing monitoring and discussing psychological well-being using the Well-being Questionnaire with the diabetes nurse specialist versus standard care. This directly compares PROMs feedback to clinicians versus no feedback.
This is a review/editorial article discussing barriers and approaches to implementing PROs in clinical practice. It is not a randomised trial and does not test PROMs feedback versus no feedback.

This is a randomized factorial experiment testing different message components (expectancy priming, autonomy support, exemplification) for tailored feedback messages. It does not compare PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals/patients vs no feedback. The intervention is about optimizing message design, not about PROMs feedback as an intervention.
This is a qualitative study (interviews with 6 health visitors), not a randomized trial. Does not meet the inclusion criteria requiring RCTs.

This is a randomized trial where patients with depressive symptoms were randomized to control or intervention group where providers were given completed PHQ-9 questionnaires (PROMs feedback). This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.
This is a validation study of a hearing self-assessment questionnaire against audiometric evaluation. It is not a randomized trial comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.
This study tests physiological feedback (heart rate visual feedback), not PROMs feedback. It is also not described as a randomized trial comparing feedback to no feedback.

This is a cluster randomized clinical trial that includes patient self-assessment (READI2 protocol) as part of the intervention. The patient self-assessment using Readiness for Hospital Discharge Scale represents PROMs feedback. This compares protocols with patient self-assessment vs without.

Although this is an RCT, clinicians received summaries of participant reports at each time point in BOTH groups (intervention and control). Therefore, this does not compare PROMs feedback to no feedback - the feedback was present in both arms.

This study describes using a self-administered depression questionnaire to alert residents to possible depression cases, but it is unclear from the abstract whether this was a randomized trial. The abstract does not clearly describe randomization or a control group without feedback.

This is a randomized trial where patients were randomized to experimental group (therapists received feedback from OQ-45 and ASC instruments) or control group (treatment-as-usual, no feedback). This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.
This is a literature review, not a primary randomized trial. Does not meet inclusion criteria.

This study evaluates a mobile phone app for syndromic surveillance (collecting symptom data for disease detection), not PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals or patients to improve outcomes. It is not an RCT comparing PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

This is a randomized controlled clinical trial where patients were assigned to intervention (HRQL assessment with feedback to clinicians via graphical representation) or control (HRQL assessment without feedback). This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

This is a pilot RCT comparing web-based self-management portal with real-time monitoring, feedback, and support from a nurse case manager vs usual care. The intervention includes PROMs feedback (symptom monitoring) to both patients and healthcare provider.

This is an RCT comparing three conditions including full screening with a personalized report summarizing concerns on the medical file (PROMs feedback) vs minimal screening (distress thermometer only without personalized report). This compares PROMs feedback to minimal/no feedback.
This is a debate/methodology paper about systematic reviewing complex interventions, not a primary RCT. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
This is an RCT about communication skills training for oncologists, not about PROMs feedback to patients or healthcare professionals. The intervention is training, not PROMs feedback.

This is a cluster RCT where primary care physicians in intervention clinics were notified of their patients' GDS scores (PROMs feedback), while physicians in control clinics were not notified. This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

This study assessed effects of providing GPs with feedback of patients' BDI scores. The BDI scores of a random 45% were disclosed to GPs. This is an RCT comparing PROMs feedback to GPs vs no feedback.

This is an RCT about a communication-priming intervention (Jumpstart-Tips) to increase goals-of-care conversations, not about PROMs feedback. The intervention is pre-conversation priming, not PROMs feedback.
This is a commentary/opinion piece by Nick Black, not a primary randomized trial. Does not meet inclusion criteria.

This is a study design/recruitment paper for an RCT that randomizes patients into 3 arms: arm 1 (patient and rheumatologist see self-assessed disease activity), arm 2 (only patient sees data), arm 3 (neither sees data). This compares PROMs feedback conditions to no feedback, meeting inclusion criteria.

This is a cluster-randomized trial comparing tailored risk information printouts vs non-tailored information about cancer risk and screening. This is about risk communication, not PROMs feedback on patient health outcomes.

This is an RCT about nurse-managed telephone follow-up after total knee arthroplasty, not about PROMs feedback to patients or healthcare professionals. The intervention is telephone calls, not PROMs feedback.
This is a systematic review of RCTs, not a primary RCT itself. Does not meet inclusion criteria for primary studies.
This is a methodology paper about the GRADE system for rating evidence quality, not a primary RCT. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
This is a conceptual/methodology paper reviewing definitions of comorbidity, not a primary RCT. Does not meet inclusion criteria.

This is an RCT comparing standard care vs SIS.NET which includes online health questionnaires (patient self-reported data/PROMs) with remote review by nurse practitioners. This compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs standard care without systematic PROMs feedback.

This paper reports on the FOCUS RCT which investigated routine completion and feedback of outcome measures for adult mental health service patients (101 intervention with feedback, 59 control without). This directly compares PROMs feedback vs no feedback.

This is a prospective RCT where physicians were randomly assigned to receive instant online graphical output of HRQoL data (intervention) vs conducted consultations as usual (control). This directly compares PROMs feedback to healthcare professionals vs no feedback.

This is an overview/survey of randomized phase III trials in prostate cancer, not a primary RCT about PROMs feedback. It analyzes whether HRQOL was reported in trials, not whether PROMs feedback improves outcomes.

This is a cluster RCT about implementing clinical practice guidelines for elderly depression through various interventions (outreach visits, website, tools, CME course). The intervention is not PROMs feedback but rather guideline implementation strategies.
This is a software advertisement for EndNote reference management software, not a research study. Does not meet inclusion criteria.
